awd_titl_txt: Travel: NSF Student Travel Grants for SOUPS 2025, VehicleSec '25, and USENIX Security '25
awd_abstract_narration:
This award will support student travel to the 33rd edition of the USENIX Security Conference and two co-located conferences: the 20th edition of the Symposium on Usable Privacy and Security (SOUPS), and the third USENIX Symposium on Vehicle Security and Privacy (VehicleSec), to be held in August 2025.  The USENIX Security Conference is one of the most important research conferences for professionals to present cutting edge research of fundamental importance to advancing understanding of computer systems security.  SOUPS is a leading venue for research on security and privacy topics as they relate to people, organizations, and society; VehicleSec is an emerging venue for research about theories, technologies, and systems related to security and privacy issues around vehicles, their sub-systems, supporting infrastructures, and related fundamental technologies.  Funding this travel will allow student researchers to connect to experts from across the academic, government, and industry communities to foster cross-disciplinary approaches and to address shared research challenges.

This award will provide travel support to about 33 students who who otherwise have limited travel funding and so might not be able to attend. The funding will allow students to present at the conference and receive valuable mentoring both at the conference and beyond, through an online community that supports attendees. Criteria for selection include financial need, conference participation, close alignment with conference topics, first-time attendance, and diversity of institutional, personal, and disciplinary backgrounds.

This award reflects NSF's statutory mission and has been deemed worthy of support through evaluation using the Foundation's intellectual merit and broader impacts review criteria.

Outcomes Report, SOUPS 2025, VehicleSec ‘25, and USENIX Security ‘25

This grant provided travel funding to assist US-based students to attend one of three USENIX events in August 2025, specifically the 21st Symposium on Usable Privacy and Security (SOUPS 2025), the Third USENIX Symposium on Vehicle Security and Privacy (VehicleSec ‘25), and the 34th USENIX Security Symposium (USENIX Security ‘25). All three events took place in Seattle, Washington. 

SOUPS 2025 took place August 10-12, 2025. SOUPS 2025 brought together an interdisciplinary group of researchers and practitioners in human-computer interaction, security, and privacy. Topics included all areas of usable privacy and security, emphasizing security or privacy functionality and design; field studies of security or privacy technology; usability evaluations of new or existing security or privacy features; security testing of new or existing usability features; lessons learned; and ethical, psychological, sociological, or anthropological aspects of usable security; and privacy. 

VehicleSec ‘25 took place August 11-12, 2025, co-located with SOUPS 2025. VehicleSec brought together an audience of university researchers, scientists, industry professionals, and government representatives to contribute new theories, technologies, and systems on any security/privacy issues related to vehicles, their sub-systems, supporting infrastructures, and related fundamental technologies. 

USENIX Security ‘25 took place August 13-15, 2025. Held annually, the USENIX Security Symposium brings together researchers, practitioners, system administrators, system programmers, and others interested in the latest advances in the security and privacy of computer systems and networks. Topics included all areas relating to systems research in security and privacy, emphasizing system security, network security, security analysis, machine learning security and privacy, data-driven security and measurement studies, privacy-enhancing technologies, language-based security, hardware security, research on surveillance and censorship, social issues, and applications of cryptography.

Participation in these and similar conferences is a valuable and important part of the graduate school experience. It provides students with the opportunity to interact with more senior researchers in the field and exposes students to leading-edge work in the field. This grant made possible the participation of students, primarily Ph.D. candidates, who would otherwise be unable to attend the conferences and extended the impact of research presented to a broad audience of young researchers from across the country. Students who participated in each event were offered activities to enhance their interactions with senior researchers and organizers, including mentoring events, a student meetup, poster sessions, and receptions. The NSF funding provided under this award allowed us to substantially increase the number of students we could support with grants at these events.

Any student enrolled full-time at an accredited US university or college was eligible to apply for a grant. Grants had two components: 1) registration costs and 2) expenses. For those students selected, USENIX covered registration costs by providing students with a registration code for full student registration. For the expense portion, USENIX provided payment to assist the student with costs related to airfare and lodging. Variations in the rates offered depended on how far a student needed to travel and the amount they requested (i.e., some students may stay with a friend in the town of the conference and therefore not have a hotel expense). We confirmed that the student recipients registered and attended the event. 

The criteria we used in selecting grant recipients included:

  • Conference participation (e.g., presenting a poster)

  • Areas of study that significantly overlapped with the conference topics

  • The pertinence of a supporting statement outlining the applicant’s research

  • Application history, prioritizing first-time applicants and those not receiving a grant in the previous twelve months

  • Students from institutions not traditionally represented at USENIX events

  • Class level, prioritizing graduate students, and financial need

The NSF funds supported 62 grants for students to participate in the three events. USENIX appreciates the continued financial support from the NSF, which allowed us to grant awards to many more qualified applicants than we would have been able to otherwise. Grants across the events are detailed below: 

  • For SOUPS 2025, USENIX received 24 grant applications from students and awarded 23 grants. The NSF funds of $15,000 covered 18 of these grants, and all those awardees were enrolled at U.S. universities. 

  • For VehicleSec ‘25, USENIX received 21 grant applications from students and awarded 15 students. NSF funds from this award, amounting to $6,000, covered 11 of these grants. All awardees were enrolled at U.S. universities. 

  • For USENIX Security ‘25, we received 144 grant applications from students and awarded 76 grants. The NSF funds of $25,000 covered 33 of these grants, and all those awardees were enrolled at U.S. universities.
